Priya / Mateo,

Quick technical notes based on BrightBank's profile (40 req/s, ~600 tokens per interaction):

1) Quantization options
- FP16: Minimal accuracy regression, best for latency-sensitive low-distortion use. Works well if you need top-tier quality; throughput improvement modest compared to int8.
- Static INT8 (per-channel quant): ~2-4x memory reduction and 1.5-2x throughput improvement on supported kernels. Expect occasional ~0.5-1% generation quality drop on longer-tail prompts; recommend running eval set.
- Mixed precision / hybrid: quantize most weights to int8, keep attention and layernorm in FP16. Good middle ground and often our default for POC workload.

2) Batching and KV cache interplay
- With 40 req/s and 600 avg tokens, continuous batching gives strong benefits. For inference SLO ~300-600ms p50, target dynamic batch windows of 5-20ms with sequence-aware batching.
- KV cache hit-rate will dominate throughput for multi-turn sessions. If BrightBank expects 60-70% session stickiness, expect 30-40% token savings from prefix/KV caching.

3) Pilot config recommendations
- Runtime: mixed-precision (int8 weights, FP16 critical ops) as baseline.
- Batch settings: max_batch_size=64, latency_window=10ms, adaptive backoff if tail latency >95th target.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching across sessions where session_id present; TTL 24h for pilot.

4) Risks / evaluation items
- Evaluate generation quality on a 200-sample eval set; report both semantic parity and token-level divergence.
- If you see >1.5% quality regression with int8, fallback to mixed precision for specific model layers.

Attaching: quant_recs_v1.pdf with eval matrix and suggested configs.

- Karthik
